'''Anca Muscholl''' (born 1967){{r|born}} is a Romanian-German [[mathematical logic]]ian and [[theoretical computer science|theoretical computer scientist]] known for her work on [[formal verification]], [[model checking]], and [[two-variable logic]]. She is a researcher at the {{ill|Laboratoire bordelais de recherche en informatique|fr}} (LaBRI), a professor at the [[University of Bordeaux]], and a former junior member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]].{{r|tum}}

==Education and career==
Muscholl was born in [[Bucharest]],{{r|diss}} came to Germany as a teenage refugee in 1984,{{r|cnrs}} and won first place in two German national mathematics competitions (the {{ill|Bundeswettbewerb Mathematik|de}}) in 1985 and 1986.{{r|tum|cnrs}} She earned a master's degree at the [[Technical University of Munich]],{{r|tum}} and completed her Ph.D. at the [[University of Stuttgart]] in 1994. Her dissertation, ''Über die Erkennbarkeit unendlicher Spuren'', was supervised by {{ill|Volker Diekert|de}} and published by Teubner Verlag in 1996.{{r|diss}} She also earned a [[habilitation]] at the University of Stuttgart in 1999.{{r|tum}}

After becoming a professor at [[Paris Diderot University]] in 1999, she moved to the University of Bordeaux in 2006.{{r|tum}}

==Recognition==
Muscholl was a junior member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]] from 2007 to 2012.{{r|tum}} She won the [[CNRS Silver Medal]] in 2010.{{r|tum|cnrs}}
